title: Loop sums
hints: Start each function with an accumulator (`sum := 0` or `count := 0`), update it in the loop, and return it. `for i := range n` runs zero times when `n <= 0`, so the edge cases come for free.

`range n` yields `0 … n-1`. For `SumTo` you need `1 … n`: either loop over `range n + 1` (adding 0 does nothing) or add `i + 1`. `SumOfMultiples` wants `k < limit`, which is exactly `range limit` — but skip `k == 0`.
In `SumOfMultiples`: `if k == 0 || (k%a != 0 && k%b != 0) { continue }` then `sum += k`. In `CountDivisors`: `if n%(i+1) == 0 { count++ }`.
